source_text.body:
Run project workflow with a Dot agent following SOPs
A user ran a project workflow through Dot, which followed SOPs at first but later became less reliable and needed more oversight.
·
Nov 17, 2026
Done with
DO
Dots
What they did
The poster used Dot as a long-running assistant for project work, expecting it to follow their SOPs and improve over time. When it started forgetting or violating those rules, they added supports around it: agent notes in other tools, plugins and skills, extra memory and code-mapping software, and scheduled tasks that watched events and fed Dot SOP-based instructions; they also rebooted it on advice from another Reddit user.
How it went
It worked well for about a week, then needed steadily more supervision, with the poster saying they spent more time policing Dot than doing the project. They report weeks or months of delay, higher server and subscription costs, and estimate they got the desired result only about a quarter of the time on a $200 plan.
Worth knowing
The main catch was upkeep: the user says they had to keep adding checkpoints, resets, and scheduled-task guardrails because Dot's memory and project isolation got worse over time.
Try it yourself
with
Dots
Copy prompt
Here are the SOPs for my [project type, e.g. client onboarding] workflow: [paste or link SOPs]. Run this workflow for [project or client name] from start to finish, following each step in order and noting what you completed. If a step is ambiguous or you'd need to send a message, submit a form, or delete anything, pause and check with me first. Each time you finish a stage, send me a short status update, and stop when all steps are done or you hit something that needs my decision.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/OpenAI/comments/1xymiei/a_letter_to_openai_about_dot
